NKE.rationale: Nike is in a deep fundamental trough with no near-term catalyst to reverse the trajectory. Q3 FY2026 (Feb 2026) showed EPS of $0.35, down 35% YoY from $0.54, with operating income collapsing to $650M from $844M. Revenue was essentially flat YoY at $11.28B but down 9.2% QoQ, signaling the 'Win Now' turnaround is not yet delivering top-line growth. Operating cash flow plunged 76% YoY to $430M. The company faces a triple headwind: (1) tariff costs of ~$1B in FY2026, (2) Greater China revenue down 30% since 2021 with no stabilization in sight, and (3) Converse declining 19% in FY2025. Gross margin compressed 130bps in Q3 due to tariffs and promotional activity. Valuation remains expensive at 30x trailing PE despite deteriorating earnings — the PE range over the past year was 19.5-38.9, and at 30x the stock is in the upper half while fundamentals are at their worst. P/B of 4.8x is near the low end of the 4.4-8.4 range, but this reflects falling ROE (now 16% vs 32% a year ago) rather than genuine cheapness. News sentiment is deeply negative (mean -0.40 over 90 days), with RBC downgrading and slashing PT to $50, JPMorgan downgrading to Underweight with $40 PT, and multiple analyst warnings that turnaround benefits won't materialize until 2027. The stock has declined for four consecutive quarters (-15% QoQ each), and consensus FY2026 EPS of $1.49 would be a 31% decline. The next earnings event (June 30) is expected to show EPS of $0.11, down 21% YoY — another leg down. There is no credible near-term fundamental catalyst; the tariff refund of ~$986M is a one-time item that doesn't fix the structural issues. This is a deteriorating business with expensive valuation and negative momentum across all three pillars.
